_note: The scenario corpus for DoDonPachi DaiOuJou. Every script is keyed on LOGIC frames (the game's own completed frames, sampled at the $803940 arm write), never on video frames -- the two come apart exactly when slowdown happens, which is the thing we are here to measure. `bootPrefix` is not optional decoration: ddpdojblk boots to a chooser whose SILENT DEFAULT is VERSION-A (2002.04.05 MASTER), so a scenario without the versionB prefix measures the wrong game.

scenarios.name: chooser
scenarios.why: the version chooser itself: prove a scripted run lands in VERSION-B and that the probe can tell which build is live from the arm PC's top nibble

scenarios.name: chooser-a
scenarios.why: the CONTROL. Identical harness, no chooser input, the ~5 s countdown expires and the game falls through. Must be running build A at the END -- not merely 'in build A', because the chooser itself is build A code.

scenarios.name: stage1-open
scenarios.why: THE GATE SCENARIO. Boot -> VERSION-B -> coin -> start -> ship select -> the opening of stage 1, firing. Everything downstream compares against this.

scenarios.name: stage1-deep
scenarios.why: a longer run into stage 1 for the load meter's dynamic range and for any (B) dilation event; the wave-0 corpus found its heaviest 55 frames around here

scenarios.name: fly-around
scenarios.why: WAVE 4. THE PORT SCENARIO. Boot -> VERSION-B -> stage 1, then 2,200 logic frames of scripted stick from the seed at lf2000: each cardinal held long enough to PIN each of the four walls (vertical $800..$6500 = 23,808 units at 246/frame = 97 frames to cross; horizontal $300..$3500 = 12,800 at 163/frame = 79), all four diagonals, single-frame reversals, and the two conflicting-stick cases the $2552DC table answers with $FF. MISSES MATTER AS MUCH AS MOVES: the clamp is move-past-then-clamp with a compensating write to the velocity accumulator, so a port that clamps first is wrong ONLY at a wall. NO BUTTONS, and that is the whole design of this scenario: mirror bit 4 (Button 1) is the shot edge at $249B48, mirror bit 5 (Button 2) is the bomb at $2497FE, and mirror bit 6 (Button 3) is AUTO-SHOT -- $2497B2 finds the byte at $80380F set to $01 and synthesises a shot edge into ($19,A6) on alternate frames -- so every button drives wave 5's code. THE INTERVENTION: $810424 (the player's ($3e,A6) invulnerability timer) is held at $FF from lf1990, at the sample point, on BOTH SIDES of the comparison. Without it a button-free run of this script DIES at lf2469 (MEASURED: the player record goes blank and the object table drops a slot), because nothing is shooting the stage-1 opening. $FF is a value the game itself writes at $2495A2 and the branch that reads it ($249524 cmpi.b #$ff) is ported, so the poke changes WHETHER the ship dies and not WHAT any ported routine computes -- the same rule wave 2 applied to the NOP sled. With it the object table is static at 8 live slots from lf1969 to lf4200, so objn/objord/objlive are real compared columns rather than a tautology.

scenarios.name: stage1-shot
scenarios.why: WAVE 8. THE SHOT SCENARIO, and every number in this description was measured before the scenario was written. The ship FIRES: single-frame taps of Button 1 (mirror bit 4, the shot edge at $249B48) every 20 logic frames. Taps, never a HOLD: holding Button 1 starts the laser speed ramp 22->12, which lives in the OPTION object ($24C8BE, A6 = the option record) and is UNPORTED, so a hold would go red on `pspd` for a reason that has nothing to do with the shot. THE COMPARED WINDOW IS lf3717..4572 AND IT WAS CHOSEN BY MEASUREMENT, on TWO conditions. $245044 (`bset #$7,(-$3,A6)`, the shot-vs-enemy damage routine) is the only writer of the shot record's HIT bit, and the hit path it gates ($253BDE / $253ECA) is deliberately NOT translated -- it needs the enemy port, which is still blocked. So $245044's per-frame execution count over the ten COMPARED records is the column `hitex`, the gate FAILS on any non-zero value inside the window. The SECOND condition is the one that is easy to miss: the hit bit is STICKY, so a record that was hit BEFORE the seed carries it into the window and the port would throw on frame one. The seed frame is therefore the earliest frame at which EVERY record in the 36-slot table has bit 7 clear AND no later frame in the run sets it on a compared record -- lf3716, giving 856 compared frames, MEASURED (the seed frames either side give 855 and 854; the best window that ignores the sticky-bit condition is 871 and throws). Over that window the PLAYER's own ten slots hold 0..6 live records (mean 3.6) and the whole table 0..16 (mean 8.6, zero on 37 frames), so both a busy table and an empty one are covered. $81295C counts the WHOLE table, including the OPTION PODS' shots in slots 0..12 -- which the board keeps respawning through the unported $24D484 and the port cannot -- so it is a REPORTED column, never a claimed one, and the runner prints how far apart the two sides drift. MOVEMENT IS VERTICAL ONLY INSIDE THE WINDOW, and that is a named gap rather than a convenience: $813176, the background's per-frame horizontal scroll delta, is read by the shot driver at $253A76 and subtracted from every live shot at $253AA6, and it is produced by $26151E inside the unported background object. MEASURED: it is 0 on every frame of this run and non-zero only while the ship crosses the screen horizontally. It is a COMPARED COLUMN, so the scroll-compensated path stays visibly untested instead of quietly rotting. The $810424=FF invulnerability intervention is the same one fly-around uses, for the same reason and at the same sample point on both sides.

scenarios.name: speedmodes
scenarios.why: WAVE 4 item: 'per-button speed modes'. The build-A memmap recon measured 246 units/frame vertical, 163 horizontal, and 313 WITH BUTTON 2 OR 3 HELD. This scenario holds each of the three buttons in turn while pushing the stick up, so the speed index ($8103E6+$1A) and the applied delta ($810416) are MEASURED on VERSION-B instead of inherited. It fires the weapons, so it is a measurement scenario, not a comparison scenario.

scenarios.name: overrun
scenarios.why: WAVE 2 ITEM 2, PERMANENT. The only scenario in the corpus in which the game runs out of time. Nobody had ever reached an overrun -- wave 0's heaviest stage-1 frames stopped at >90% utilised and wave 1's gate completed its loop on all 2,600 frames -- so mechanism (C) was unmeasured, and docs/knowledge/06 says (C) cannot be retrofitted. MAME's -speed is a HOST throttle and changes no emulated cycle; a per-CPU clock scale is not reachable from MAME 0.288's Lua (measured). So a busy-wait trampoline is written into the decrypted image past the end of the program and one main-loop jsr operand is repointed at it: `inject` is NOPS:fromLogicFrame (a NOP sled: no register, no flag, no memory touched). It preserves D0, touches no game RAM, and changes WHEN the frame runs out of time, never WHAT the game does about it. `pgm.py overrun` runs the NOPS=0 control first, which MUST be byte-identical to the unpatched run. EVERY NUMBER FROM THIS SCENARIO IS MAME-TIMED, UNCALIBRATED, AND A MECHANISM RESULT ONLY.

scenarios.name: stage1-sweep
scenarios.why: WAVE 69. THE WHOLE OF STAGE 1, ONCE, so that everything downstream is a JavaScript re-seed rather than another emulator run. Stage 1 is 7,317 logic frames to the boss lock and the boss's own $294F32 timeout ends it at lf19,218 (W62), and NOTHING IN THIS REPO HAS EVER COMPARED PAST lf6,185: every art, coverage and divergence figure this project holds was measured over 3,000-6,185 frames from boot, and the owner reports the picture degrading progressively AFTER THE MIDBOSS DIES (~lf3800-4200) -- i.e. the trouble starts almost exactly where the measurement window ends. MEASURED this wave: MAME does 23 logic frames per second of wall clock with -video none, so this run costs ~14 minutes ONCE and every later comparison costs nothing. THE INTERVENTION, LABELLED: $810424 (the player's ($3e,A6) invulnerability timer) is held at $FF from lf1890 on BOTH sides, exactly as `fly-around` does and for the same reason -- without it a scripted run dies long before the stage ends and the deep frames cannot be reached at all. docs/knowledge/09 is explicit that this gives STATES, not a picture of the game: an invulnerable run produces game states a player cannot produce (no death, no respawn, no rank drop) and is valid FOR COVERAGE ONLY. The companion scenario `stage1-sweep-natural` is the same script with no poke and exists to MEASURE where a scripted player actually dies, which is the number this one cannot produce. AUTO-SHOT, not tapped fire: Button 3 (mirror bit 6) is the auto-shot the corpus's own `stage1-open` and `stage1-deep` already hold, so the ship is FIRING for the whole stage (owner decision 4: a passive run is pinned at minimum rank with nothing dying -- a different game). Movement is `tailRepeat`, an eight-phase 240-frame cycle, because a literal 19,000-frame script would not fit in a Windows environment block.

scenarios.name: stage1-play
scenarios.why: WAVE 69. THE DEEP PORT SCENARIO -- the whole of stage 1 with an input sequence THE PORT CAN ACTUALLY FOLLOW, which `stage1-sweep` turned out not to be. MEASURED this wave, seeding the port at lf4000 of `stage1-sweep`: the port BLOCKS on its very first frame at the named throw $2497AA, the unported $2497BA hyper/auto block, because that block is gated on (operator byte $80380F non-zero) AND (mirror bit 6 held) -- and mirror bit 6 is Button 3, the AUTO-SHOT that `stage1-open`, `stage1-deep`, `overrun` and `stage1-sweep` all hold. $80380F is $01 on this cartridge. So FOUR scenarios in this corpus hold a button the port cannot process, and nobody had noticed, because all four are BOARD-ONLY scenarios (the determinism gate and the load meter) that had never been handed to the port. This one fires with SINGLE-FRAME TAPS of Button 1 (mirror bit 4, the shot edge at $249B48) every 40 logic frames: taps and not a hold, because holding Button 1 starts the laser speed ramp inside the OPTION object ($24C8BE), which is unported and would go red on `pspd` for a reason that is nothing to do with the stage. THE INTERVENTION, LABELLED: $810424 held at $FF from lf1890 on BOTH sides -- the player is INVULNERABLE, so this run produces STATES, not a picture of the game (docs/knowledge/09), and it is valid FOR COVERAGE ONLY. Its companion control is `stage1-sweep-natural`.

scenarios.name: stage1-sweep-natural
scenarios.why: WAVE 69, THE CONTROL. Byte for byte the same script as `stage1-sweep` WITH NO POKE. It exists to answer the one question the invulnerable run cannot: how far into stage 1 does a scripted player actually get before dying? Measurement proves presence, so this reports a frame number and not a claim about the stage.

scenarios.name: stage1-laser-hold
scenarios.why: WAVE 75. THE OWNER'S OWN SCENARIO, verbatim: "launch an oracle backed run where you sit at the bottom of the screen and just shoot your laser. That way you should kill the mid boss. Then those invisible things you hit should appear." The ship is PARKED ON THE BOTTOM WALL AT THE HORIZONTAL CENTRE and Button 1 is HELD for the whole stage, so the LASER is up continuously and nothing else is pressed. EVERY NUMBER IN THIS SCRIPT WAS MEASURED ON THE BOARD BEFORE THE SCRIPT WAS WRITTEN (out/w75/probe.tsv, walls.tsv, step.tsv): the player record DOES NOT EXIST until lf1968, so an earlier press moves nothing (a 150-frame D from lf1750 left py at its $1179 spawn value); the vertical wall pair is $800 = THE BOTTOM (confirmed on a framebuffer PNG, not inferred) and $6500 = the top; the horizontal pair is $300 left and $3500 right, centre $1C00; and holding Button 1 drives the speed index down its laser ramp 22->12 by lf2052, at which index the horizontal step is EXACTLY 63 units per frame. So: 1970=DA brings the ship to the bottom wall with the laser already ramping; 2200=DAL pins the LEFT wall (200 frames, measured to pin by lf2399); 2400=DAR steps right for 102 frames; 2502=DA parks it at px=$1C1A -- 26 units, 0.2 % of the playfield width, about half a pixel right of the $1C00 centre, the closest an integer number of 63-unit steps can land. D STAYS HELD for the rest of the run and that is deliberate: it is what 'sitting at the bottom' means, it pins the ship so no recoil can drift it, and it keeps the input word constant for 17,000 frames. NOT Button 3: the auto-shot is mirror bit 6 and $2497B2 finds $80380F = $01 on this cartridge, so the port blocks on its first frame (W69 section 4). NOT a tap: the owner asked for the LASER, and the ramp at $24C8BE is ported (W51). THE INTERVENTION, LABELLED: $810424 (the player's ($3e,A6) invulnerability timer) is held at $FF from lf1960 on BOTH sides of every comparison. WITHOUT IT THIS EXACT SCRIPT DIES AT lf2426 (measured: pst 32768 -> 36864 -> 256, respawn at lf2499) -- a ship parked on the bottom wall is a stationary target. docs/knowledge/09: this run yields STATES, not a picture of the game, and it is SCRIPTED INPUT, NOT A HUMAN PLAYING. Its companion control is stage1-laser-hold-natural.

scenarios.name: stage1-laser-hold-natural
scenarios.why: WAVE 75, THE CONTROL FOR stage1-laser-hold. Byte for byte the same script -- park on the bottom wall at centre, hold the laser -- WITH NO POKE. It answers the one question an invulnerable run cannot: how long does a ship that sits still at the bottom of stage 1 with the laser up actually live? Measurement proves presence, so this reports a frame number and never a claim about the stage. Shorter than its twin ON PURPOSE: the answer is a death frame, and running past it buys nothing.

scenarios.name: stage2-laser-hold
scenarios.why: WAVE 431. THE STAGE-2 TWIN OF `stage1-laser-hold`, AND IT EXISTS BECAUSE THAT LADDER IS TOO SHORT, NOT BECAUSE STAGE 2 WAS UNREACHED. `stage1-laser-hold` ALREADY reaches stage 2: $813092 goes 0 -> 1 between lf10300 and lf10400 and stays there, so 92 of its 210 rungs are stage-2 rungs and 17 carry the STAGE-2 BOSS (type $30, $297120) with its 23 type-$4D satellites. WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG WITH IT: [M] the boss's main HP ($16,A5) falls 179,648 -> 142,598 across lf18000..lf19500 and the run then ENDS at lf19600, so it holds only the first fifth of the fight. THIS LADDER RUNS 30,000 FRAMES AND HOLDS ALL OF IT: [M] the boss arrives lf17900, damage starts lf18600, the PHASE TRANSITION fires between lf20600 and lf20700 -- main HP 62,456 -> 61,088, crossing $EFC0 = 61,376, exactly the `($16,A5) - $EFC0 < 0` gate at `$298926`, and all four parts go dead together (HP $FFFF, dead flags 1111) -- the boss DIES at lf21600 (main HP 288 -> negative), its record is gone by lf22000 and STAGE 3 starts at lf22300. 281 of 281 rungs, 1717 s, 17.5 logic frames per wall second. TWO THINGS IN THIS SCRIPT WERE WRONG WHEN IT WAS WRITTEN AND THE LADDER MEASURED BOTH -- READ THIS BEFORE COPYING IT. (1) THE PLAYER IS FROZEN ACROSS THE HANDOVER: [M] px sits at $E00 from lf10033 to lf10334, 301 frames, and no input moves it, so this script's `10100=DAL` fell entirely inside the freeze and pinned nothing. (2) THE 63-UNIT STEP DOES NOT APPLY THERE: the speed index is re-raised over the handover and ramps back down, so the first steps after lf10335 measure 115, 115, 115, 110, 105 units and only later settle at 63. So `10300=DAR` started from $E00 rather than the left wall and at the wrong step, and the ship parks at px $26A4 -- RIGHT of the $1C00 centre, not on it. THAT TURNED OUT NOT TO MATTER FOR THE BODY and the ladder is good: from $26A4 the body takes 60 HP per frame against the old ladder's 24.7, which is why the fight completes. It DOES still matter for the four PART hitboxes, which hold at $5000 until the phase transition kills them wholesale: the parts sit at body X +/- $6C0 and +/- $CC0 and no single parked column covers one for long. A LATER WAVE THAT WANTS THE PARTS SHOULD USE `10340=DAL;10640=DAR;10742=DA` -- after the freeze and after the ramp settles, where a wall pin is step-size-independent and 102 steps of 63 from $300 land $1C1A. WHAT THIS LADDER DOES NOT GIVE, STATED SO NOBODY MEASURES IT AGAIN: POOL-A DISPATCH INDICES 3 AND 4 ARE STILL NEVER ALLOCATED. [M] a seeded sweep of all 119 stage-2 rungs here (11,825 logic frames, 1 blocked) sees indices 0, 1 and 2 only, and the same sweep over `stage1-laser-hold`'s 92 stage-2 rungs (9,200 frames, 0 blocked) sees 0, 1, 2 and 8. Kind 4 needs `$279990`, which is behind type $90's `hp < cooldown` damage-threshold gate, and [M] type $90 sits at hp $1000 against cooldown $0 for its whole life. Kind 3 needs `$279D64` or `$279F3C`, the death tails of types $92 and $93, behind `($1,A6)` bit 7. All three types are LIVE on this route; none reaches the required sub-state from a ship parked on the bottom wall. A STAGE-2 RUNG WAS NEVER WHAT BLOCKED THEM. AND ONE THING IT FOUND: the port takes a NAMED THROW at `$23D6AC` on lf21826, 226 frames after the boss dies, in the death explosion (pool B is at 40 records) -- a display-list zoom field carry. Only a ladder that covers the boss's DEATH can reach it. THE INTERVENTION IS THE SAME ONE, LABELLED THE SAME WAY: $810424 held at $FF from lf1960; this ladder yields STATES, not a picture of the game, and it is SCRIPTED INPUT, NOT A HUMAN PLAYING (docs/knowledge/09).
